description: Speed up `task-mgr curate dedup`: replace single-linkage embedding pre-clustering with pair-centric candidate generation at a per-profile calibrated cosine threshold, capped batch grouping, pair-stable dismissals, concurrency 4, and one-time embedding normalization. Approved plan: ~/.claude/plans/plan-out-the-changes-glistening-pnueli.md

priorityPhilosophy.description: Hierarchy of what matters most when implementing tasks
hierarchy: 1. PLAN — Anticipate edge cases before coding
2. PHASE 2 FOUNDATION — ~1 day now to save ~2+ weeks later (1:10+ ratio); we are pre-launch, foundations compound
3. FUNCTIONING CODE — Pragmatic, reliable, wired in per plan
4. CORRECTNESS — Compiles, type-checks, scoped tests pass deterministically
5. CODE QUALITY — Clean code, qualityDimensions satisfied, no warnings
principles: Quality dimensions explicit — qualityDimensions on every task tells you what 'good' looks like
Edge cases = test cases — every known edge case must have a corresponding test
Scoped per-iteration tests, full suite at REVIEW-001 — REVIEW must leave the trunk green including pre-existing failures
Determinism is a feature: batch construction must be identical across runs for the same DB state (integer ordering only, no float-order or HashMap-iteration dependence)
Ship working code with tests to prove it; handle Option/Result explicitly; avoid unwrap() in production

prohibitedOutcomes: Tests that only assert 'no crash' or check type without verifying content
Tests that mirror implementation internals (break when refactoring)
Batch construction that depends on HashMap iteration order or float comparison ordering (non-deterministic across runs)
Recording dismissals for pairs the LLM never saw (below-cosine-threshold pairs must NEVER enter dedup_dismissals)
Backward-compatibility shims for --pair-mode (repo rule: just change the code)
Error messages that don't identify what went wrong
Catch-all error handlers that swallow context

globalAcceptanceCriteria.description: These criteria apply to ALL implementation tasks
criteria: Scoped tests pass: `cargo test --lib commands::curate` and `cargo test --lib learnings::embeddings`

userStories.title: Pair-generation primitives in dedup.rs + unit tests
userStories.description:
Add the additive pair-centric building blocks to src/commands/curate/dedup.rs. Old cluster code stays untouched (deleted in FEAT-003).

DO: Implement (1) `pub fn normalize_embeddings(embeddings: &mut [(i64, Vec<f32>)])` — L2-normalize in place, leave zero vectors untouched; (2) private `fn dot(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32` returning 0.0 on length mismatch (preserves the mixed-dims guard semantics of cosine_similarity); (3) `pub fn generate_candidate_pairs(normalized: &[(i64, Vec<f32>)], threshold: f32) -> Vec<(i64, i64)>` — all pairs with dot >= threshold, each emitted as normalized (lo, hi), output sorted ascending by (lo, hi); (4) `pub fn group_pairs_into_batches(pairs: &[(i64, i64)], max_items: usize, max_pairs: usize) -> Vec<Vec<(i64, i64)>>` — capped union-find grouping (reuse the existing private UnionFind; union only when the merged component would hold <= max_items distinct items; a pair whose union would exceed the cap is deterministically appended to lo's component as a bridge pair) then deterministic packing (components ordered by min member id; greedy fill enforcing <= max_pairs pairs AND <= max_items distinct items per batch; whole small components may coalesce into one batch). (5) Consts `pub const MAX_ITEMS_PER_BATCH: usize = 20;` and `pub const MAX_PAIRS_PER_BATCH: usize = 30;`.

DO NOT: Modify cosine_similarity in src/learnings/embeddings/mod.rs (other callers need the full non-normalized form). Do NOT delete cluster_by_embedding_similarity yet. Do NOT use HashMap iteration order anywhere in batch construction.

Known-bad to guard against: sorting pairs by similarity score (float) breaks determinism when scores tie — order by integer (lo, hi) only. A union-find WITHOUT the size cap recreates the exact giant-component bug this plan removes.

Unit test: threshold boundary is >= inclusive (pair at exactly the threshold IS a candidate; verify with vectors whose dot is exactly the threshold value)
Unit test: output of generate_candidate_pairs is sorted ascending and identical across two invocations (determinism)
Unit test: zero vector never matches anything (normalize leaves it zero; dot with it is 0.0)
Unit test: mixed-dims pair (1024 vs 512) yields dot 0.0, never a candidate, never a panic
Unit test: group_pairs_into_batches — no produced batch exceeds max_pairs pairs or max_items distinct items (property-style assertion over a generated pair set)

Known-bad: a 50-item mutually-similar chain (every adjacent pair a candidate) must NOT produce one giant batch — assert every batch respects the item cap; this is the anti-regression replacing test_cluster_transitivity
Unit test: pairs (A,B) and (B,C) land in the same batch when under caps (transitive-merge quality preserved)
Unit test: bridge-pair assignment is deterministic — same input twice yields byte-identical batch structure
Positive: normalize_embeddings makes every non-zero vector unit-length (assert |norm - 1.0| < 1e-5)

userStories.title: Orchestrator swap to pair-centric default; remove --pair-mode; delete cluster fn
userStories.description:
Rewire curate_dedup's embedding path onto the FEAT-002 primitives, make pair prompts the only embedding-path mode, and delete the old cluster machinery. Update existing tests mechanically.

DO: In mod.rs build Vec<DedupBatchInput> directly (replacing the two-pass Vec<Vec<Item>> + filter at :788-956). Embedding path: split embedded/unembedded as today -> normalize_embeddings -> generate_candidate_pairs(params.cosine_threshold) -> partition by dismissals.contains into (pairs_skipped_dismissed, live) with candidate_pairs_total = live + skipped -> group_pairs_into_batches(live, MAX_ITEMS_PER_BATCH, params.batch_size.unwrap_or(MAX_PAIRS_PER_BATCH).max(1)) -> per batch: items = distinct referenced ids sorted asc resolved via item_map, candidate_pairs: Some(batch_pairs), already_judged_distinct: vec![]. Replace the pre-filter ui::emit summary with pair stats (candidate pairs total / dismissed / batch count / unembedded count). Fallback paths (unembedded remainder, zero embeddings, empty embed_model): build_standard_batches + existing is_fully_dismissed skip + dismissed_pairs_within disclosure, candidate_pairs: None — clusters_skipped now counts only fallback batches. Replace batch_item_ids (:967) with batch_judged_pairs: Vec<Vec<(i64,i64)>> (pair batches -> their candidates; fallback batches -> unordered_pairs(ids).collect()). Change compute_dismissal_pairs first param from batch_ids: &[i64] to judged_pairs: &[(i64,i64)] (body iterates them; early-return on empty; fallback call sites pass unordered_pairs(...).collect() so fallback behavior is byte-identical). Update batch-summary logging (:977-1001) to pair-batch vs fallback-batch counts. Populate new DedupResult fields (0 on fallback-only path and the :747 empty short-circuit). Delete: cluster_by_embedding_similarity + its 6 in-file tests, unjudged_pairs_within + its test, DedupParams.pair_mode, the --pair-mode CLI arg and main.rs plumbing, the SKETCH STATUS doc paragraph on build_pair_judgment_prompt. Reword the pair prompt line 'has already been examined in a prior dedup run and determined to NOT be duplicates' framing to 'has already been ruled out — do not revisit those' (non-candidates may merely be below the cosine threshold, not LLM-judged). types.rs: DedupResult gains #[serde(default)] candidate_pairs_total: usize and #[serde(default)] pairs_skipped_dismissed: usize. output.rs format_dedup_text: add '{total} candidate pair(s), {skipped} previously dismissed' line when candidate_pairs_total > 0. Update the --batch-size clap help text in src/cli/commands.rs to document its dual meaning: max candidate PAIRS per LLM batch on the embedding path (default 30); learnings per batch on the fallback path (default auto).

DO NOT: Apply finalize_dedup_batch to pair batches (dismissed pairs are already excluded upstream). Do NOT record dismissals for below-threshold pairs. Do NOT change process_batches_parallel (it already dispatches the pair prompt for candidate_pairs: Some). Do NOT alter the merge_map rewrite or prior_merged_ids filtering logic in the post-LLM loop.

userStories.title: Embedding-path integration tests (pair pipeline e2e)
userStories.description:
Add the six new integration tests exercising the pair-centric embedding path end-to-end, using the existing mock CLAUDE_BINARY harness plus store_embedding to plant synthetic vectors so the embedding path activates (existing e2e tests never store embeddings and thus only cover the fallback path).

DO: Follow the existing orchestration-test pattern in tests.rs (:3258+): DEDUP_ENV_MUTEX guard, mock claude script fixture, temp DB. Plant synthetic embeddings with obvious geometry (e.g. unit vectors: A=B direction, C=D direction, orthogonal across groups) via store_embedding so candidate pairs are exactly known.

Tests: (1) pair-path e2e — prompt captured by the mock contains 'CANDIDATE PAIRS:' listing ONLY the above-threshold pairs; merge occurs; dismissals recorded only for candidate pairs (assert below-threshold cross pairs absent from dedup_dismissals). (2) dismissal stability — first run with mock returning [] dismisses all candidates; second run makes ZERO LLM invocations (mock records invocation count) and reports pairs_skipped_dismissed == candidate_pairs_total. (3) merge + rewrite — mock merges {A,B}->N while (A,C) is also a candidate in the same batch; recorded dismissal is normalized (N,C). (4) mixed corpus — embedded + unembedded learnings: both batch kinds produced (mock sees one pair prompt and one cluster prompt), both counted. (5) --batch-size 1 — each mock invocation's prompt contains exactly one candidate pair. (6) cross-batch bridge overlap — construct a pair set where the item cap forces one shared item X into TWO batches (bridge-pair rule); mock merges {X,Y} in the batch processed first; assert the second batch's cluster containing X is skipped by the existing merged_ids guard (no double merge, X retired exactly once) and that the second batch's dismissal recording stays consistent (pairs touching X recorded per the prior_merged_ids filter — i.e. NOT recorded, since X was merged by a strictly earlier batch).

DO NOT: Assert on internal batch ordering beyond determinism guarantees. Do NOT use real Ollama — embeddings are planted directly in the DB.
